Format.title: Format version
Format.description: The format version. You should always use the latest version to enable the latest features and avoid obsolete behavior.

@errorMessages.const: Incorrect value '@value'. This should be set to the latest format version, currently '1.15.0'.

ConfigSchema.title: Config schema
ConfigSchema.description: Defines the config.json format, to support more complex mods.

AllowValues.title: Allowed values
AllowValues.description:
The values the player can provide, as a comma-delimited string. If omitted, any value is allowed.
Tip: for a boolean flag, use "true, false".

AllowBlank.title: Allow blank
AllowBlank.description: Whether the field can be left blank. If false or omitted, blank fields will be replaced with the default value.

AllowMultiple.title: Allow multiple values
AllowMultiple.description: Whether the player can specify multiple comma-delimited values. Default false.

Default.title: Default value
Default.description: The default values when the field is missing. Can contain multiple comma-delimited values if AllowMultiple is true. If omitted, blank fields are left blank.

@errorMessages.const: If 'AllowBlank' is false, the 'Default' field is required.

DynamicTokens.title: Dynamic tokens
DynamicTokens.description: Custom tokens that you can use.

Name.title: Name
Name.description: The name of the token to use for tokens & conditions.

Value.title: Token value
Value.description: The value(s) to set. This can be a comma-delimited value to give it multiple values. If any block for a token name has multiple values, it will only be usable in conditions. This field supports tokens, including dynamic tokens defined before this entry.

When.title: When
When.description: Only set the value if the given conditions match. If not specified, always matches.

Changes.title: Changes
Changes.description: The changes you want to make. Each entry is called a patch, and describes a specific action to perform: replace this file, copy this image into the file, etc. You can list any number of patches.

Action.title: Action
Action.description: The kind of change to make.

Target.title: Target asset
Target.description: The game asset you want to patch (or multiple comma-delimited assets). This is the file path inside your game's Content folder, without the file extension or language (like Animals/Dinosaur to edit Content/Animals/Dinosaur.xnb). This field supports tokens and capitalization doesn't matter. Your changes are applied in all languages unless you specify a language condition.

not.const: Invalid target; it shouldn't include the 'Content/' folder, '.xnb' extension, or locale code.

LogName.title: Patch log name
LogName.description: A name for this patch shown in log messages. This is very useful for understanding errors; if not specified, will default to a name like 'entry #14 (EditImage Animals/Dinosaurs)'.

Enabled.title: Enabled
Enabled.description: Whether to apply this patch. Default true. This fields supports immutable tokens (e.g. config tokens) if they return true/false.

@errorMessages.const: Invalid value; must be true, false, or a single token which evaluates to true or false.

FromFile.title: Source file
FromFile.description: The relative file path in your content pack folder to load instead (like 'assets/dinosaur.png'). This can be a .json (data), .png (image), .tbin or .tmx (map), or .xnb file. This field supports tokens and capitalization doesn't matter.

allOf.const: Invalid value; must not contain directory climbing (like '../').
Invalid value; must be a file path ending with .json, .png, .tbin, .tmx, or .xnb.

FromArea.title: Source area
FromArea.description: The part of the source image to copy. Defaults to the whole source image.

ToArea.title: Destination area
ToArea.description: The part of the target image to replace. Defaults to the FromArea size starting from the top-left corner.

PatchMode.title: Patch mode
PatchMode.description: How to apply FromArea to ToArea. Defaults to Replace.

Fields.title: Fields
Fields.description: The individual fields you want to change for existing entries. This field supports tokens in field keys and values. The key for each field is the field index (starting at zero) for a slash-delimited string, or the field name for an object.

Entries.title: Entries
Entries.description:
The entries in the data file you want to add, replace, or delete. If you only want to change a few fields, use Fields instead for best compatibility with other mods. To add an entry, just specify a key that doesn't exist; to delete an entry, set the value to null (like "some key": null). This field supports tokens in entry keys and values.
Caution: some XNB files have extra fields at the end for translations; when adding or replacing an entry for all locales, make sure you include the extra fields to avoid errors for non-English players.

MoveEntries.title: Move entries
MoveEntries.description: Change the entry order in a list asset like Data/MoviesReactions. (Using this with a non-list asset will cause an error, since those have no order.)

ID.title: ID
ID.description: The ID of the entry to move

BeforeID.title: Before ID
BeforeID.description: Move entry so it's right before this ID

AfterID.title: After ID
AfterID.description: Move entry so it's right after this ID

ToPosition.title: To position
ToPosition.description: Move entry so it's right at this position

@errorMessages._anyOf: You must specify one of 'AfterID', 'BeforeID', or 'ToPosition'.

anyOf.const: If 'BeforeID' is specified, only 'ID' and 'BeforeID' fields are valid.
If 'AfterID' is specified, only 'ID' and 'AfterID' fields are valid.
If 'ToPosition' is specified, only 'ID' and 'ToPosition' fields are valid.

MapProperties.title: Map properties
MapProperties.description: The map properties (not tile properties) to add, replace, or delete. To add an property, just specify a key that doesn't exist; to delete an entry, set the value to null (like "some key": null). This field supports tokens in property keys and values.

MapTiles.title: Map tiles
MapTiles.description: The individual map tiles to add, edit, or remove.

Layer.description: The map layer name to change.

Position.description: The tile coordinates to change. You can use the Debug Mode mod to see tile coordinates in-game.

SetTilesheet.title: Set tilesheet
SetTilesheet.description: Sets the tilesheet ID for the tile index.

SetIndex.title: Set tile index
SetIndex.description: Sets the tile index in the tilesheet.

SetProperties.title: Set tile properties
SetProperties.description: The properties to set or remove. This is merged into the existing tile properties, if any. To remove a property, set its value to `null` (not "null" in quotes).

Remove.description: Whether to remove the current tile and all its properties on that layer. If combined with the other fields, a new tile is created from the other fields as if the tile didn't previously exist.

When.title: When
When.description: Only apply the patch if the given conditions match.

FromFile.description:
The relative path to the map in your content pack folder from which to copy (like assets/town.tbin). This can be a .tbin, .tmx, or .xnb file. This field supports tokens and capitalization doesn't matter.
Content Patcher will handle tilesheets referenced by the FromFile map for you:
 - If a tilesheet isn't referenced by the target map, Content Patcher will add it for you (with a z_ ID prefix to avoid conflicts with hardcoded game logic). If the source map has a custom version of a tilesheet that's already referenced, it'll be added as a separate tilesheet only used by your tiles.
 - If you include the tilesheet file in your mod folder, Content Patcher will use that one automatically; otherwise it will be loaded from the game's Content/Maps folder.

FromArea.description: The part of the source map to copy. Defaults to the whole source map.

ToArea.description: The part of the target map to replace.

chrome_url_overrides.description: Override pages are a way to substitute an HTML file from your extension for a page that Google Chrome normally provides.

bookmarks.description: The page that appears when the user chooses the Bookmark Manager menu item from the Chrome menu or, on Mac, the Bookmark Manager item from the Bookmarks menu. You can also get to this page by entering the URL chrome://bookmarks.

history.description: The page that appears when the user chooses the History menu item from the Chrome menu or, on Mac, the Show Full History item from the History menu. You can also get to this page by entering the URL chrome://history.

newtab.description: The page that appears when the user creates a new tab or window. You can also get to this page by entering the URL chrome://newtab.

commands.description: Use the commands API to add keyboard shortcuts that trigger actions in your extension, for example, an action to open the browser action or send a command to the extension.

content_scripts.description: Content scripts are JavaScript files that run in the context of web pages.

exclude_matches.description: Excludes pages that this content script would otherwise be injected into.

match_about_blank.description: Whether to insert the content script on about:blank and about:srcdoc.

devtools_page.description: A DevTools extension adds functionality to the Chrome DevTools. It can add new UI panels and sidebars, interact with the inspected page, get information about network requests, and more.

externally_connectable.description: Declares which extensions, apps, and web pages can connect to your extension via runtime.connect and runtime.sendMessage.

items.description: The IDs of extensions or apps that are allowed to connect. If left empty or unspecified, no extensions or apps can connect.
The URL patterns for web pages that are allowed to connect. This does not affect content scripts. If left empty or unspecified, no web pages can connect.

accepts_tls_channel_id.description: Indicates that the extension would like to make use of the TLS channel ID of the web page connecting to it. The web page must also opt to send the TLS channel ID to the extension via setting includeTlsChannelId to true in runtime.connect's connectInfo or runtime.sendMessage's options.

file_browser_handlers.description: You can use this API to enable users to upload files to your website.

oauth2.description: Use the Chrome Identity API to authenticate users: the getAuthToken for users logged into their Google Account and the launchWebAuthFlow for users logged into a non-Google account.

optional_permissions.description: Use the chrome.permissions API to request declared optional permissions at run time rather than install time, so users understand why the permissions are needed and grant only those that are necessary.

options_page.description: To allow users to customize the behavior of your extension, you may wish to provide an options page. If you do, a link to it will be provided from the extensions management page at chrome://extensions. Clicking the Options link opens a new tab pointing at your options page.

chrome_style.description: If true, a Chrome user agent stylesheet will be applied to your options page. The default value is false, but we recommend you enable it for a consistent UI with Chrome.

open_in_tab.description: If true, your extension's options page will be opened in a new tab rather than embedded in chrome://extensions. The default is false, and we recommend that you don't change it. This is only useful to delay the inevitable deprecation of the old options UI! It will be removed soon, so try not to use it. It will break.

permissions.description: Permissions help to limit damage if your extension or app is compromised by malware. Some permissions are also displayed to users before installation, as detailed in Permission Warnings.

sandbox.description: Defines an collection of app or extension pages that are to be served in a sandboxed unique origin, and optionally a Content Security Policy to use with them.

short_name.description: The short name is typically used where there is insufficient space to display the full name.

update_url.description: If you publish using the Chrome Developer Dashboard, ignore this field. If you host your own extension or app: URL to an update manifest XML file.

tts_engine.description: Register itself as a speech engine.

voice_name.description: Identifies the name of the voice and the engine used.

schema.title: Query
schema.description: A JSON format to support searching for collections in the CMR.

QueryCondition.description: Condition used to filter collection search results from the CMR. If multiple properties are provided in a single condition they will be implicitly AND'ed.

and.description: Groups together conditions to return the intersection of the results.

or.description: Groups together conditions to return the union of the results.

provider.description: UMM Provider

updated_since.description: Revisions with revision date later than provided value

version.description: UMM Version

oneOf.description: Concept ID searches are always case sensitive

tag.description: Search against the subfields of associated tag.

platform.description: Search against any of the subfields in the platform hierarchy

category.description: Top level classification of platforms.

series_entity.description: Second level classification under category. These keywords usually (but not always) refer to a series of Earth or space observing satellites.

short_name.description: Abbreviated name of the platform (source) used to acquire the data.

long_name.description: Full name of the platform (source) used to acquire the data.

uuid.description: Unique identifier for the platform within the GCMD Keyword Management System.

any.description: Search against any of the platform subfields (category, series_entity, etc.) for the provided value.

instrument.description: Search against any of the subfields in the instrument hierarchy

category.description: Top level classification of instruments.

type.description: Third level classification under class.

short_name.description: Abbreviated name of the instrument used to acquire the data.

long_name.description: Full name of the instrument used to acquire the data.

uuid.description: Unique identifier for the instrument within the GCMD Keyword Management System.

any.description: Search against any of the instrument subfields (category, class, etc.) for the provided value.

data_center.description: Search for data centers of any type (archive, distribution, processing, and originating are all searched.)

archive_center.description: Search for data centers with a type of archive center.

location_keyword.description: Search against any of the subfields in the UMM location keyword hierarchy

category.description: Top level classification of locations.

type.description: Second level classification under category.

uuid.description: Unique identifier for the location keyword within the GCMD Keyword Management System.

detailed_location.description: Filter collections by the detailed location subfield within UMM location keywords.

any.description: Search against any of the location keyword subfields (category, type, etc.) for the provided value.

two_d_coordinate_system_name.description: UMM two dimensional coordinate system name

keyword.description: Used for free text search across most search fields. Refer to the section 'Find collections by keyword search' on https://cmr.earthdata.nasa.gov/search/site/search_api_docs.html for a list of all fields searched against. Searches are always case insensitive and treat '?' and '*' as wild-cards.

uuid.description: Unique identifier for the science keyword within the GCMD Keyword Management System.

any.description: Search against any of the science keyword subfields (category, term, etc.) for the provided value.

doi.description: Specifies a Digital Object Identifier search.

recurring_start_day.description: An integer representing the day to get collections with a temporal extent over a recurring annual period starting on or after the given day.

recurring_end_day.description: An integer representing the day to get collections with a temporal extent over a recurring annual period ending on or before the given day.

exclude_boundary.description: If set to true, the search will not include the boundary date times. It has no impact on periodic temporal searches. Defaults to false.

additional_attribute_name.description: Search for additional attributes by name and/or group. One of name or group is required.

additional_attribute_value.description: Search for additional attributes by an exact value.

value.description: Search for an exact value.

additional_attribute_range.description: Search for additional attributes by range. One of min_value or max_value are required in addition to name and type.

min_value.description: Search for values for an additional attribute which are greater than the provided value.

max_value.description: Search for values for an additional attribute which are less than the provided value.

exclude_boundary.description: If set to true, the search will not include the boundary values for min and max values. Defaults to false.

StringCondition.description: String searches can take either a string or an object with a value to search for and options to apply for the search.

oneOf.description: Used to specify the value and options to apply when searching against a particular field. 'value' is required.

value.description: The value to search for the given field.

CaseInsensitiveStringCondition.description: String searches can take either a string or an object with a value to search for and options to apply for the search. This is similar to StringCondition, but it does not support ignore_case options.

oneOf.description: Used to specify the value and options to apply when searching against a particular field. 'value' is required.

value.description: The value to search for the given field.

oneOf.description: Must contain 4 numbers in the following order: west, south, east, north. West and east represent longitudes (-180 to 180), south and north represent latitudes (-90 to 90).

AttributeGroupCondition.description: Additional attribute group, which is generally a namespace.

AttributeTypeCondition.description: The data type of the attribute being searched against.

AttributeValueCondition.description: An attribute value to search against.

DataCenterCondition.description: Search against any of the subfields in the data center hierarchy

level_0.description: Top level classification of data centers.

short_name.description: Abbreviated name of the data center.

long_name.description: The full name of the data center.

url.description: The Uniform Resource Locator (URL) of the data center.

uuid.description: Unique identifier for the data center within the GCMD Keyword Management System.

any.description: Search against any of the data center subfields (level0, url, etc.) for the provided value.

TagCondition.description: Search against the subfields of tags associated with the collection

originator_id.description: Originator id of the associated tag.

IgnoreCaseOption.description: If set to true, the search will be case insensitive and if set to false, the search will be case sensitive. Defaults to true.

PatternOption.description: If set to true, the search will treat the value provided for the given field as a pattern with wild-cards, in which '*' matches zero or more characters and '?' matches any single character.

cors.description: Configures Cross Origin Resource Sharing for public endpoints.

allow_credentials.description: Sets whether the request can include user credentials like cookies, HTTP authentication or client side SSL certificates.

max_age.description: Sets how long (in seconds) the results of a preflight request can be cached. If set to 0, every request is preceded by a preflight request.

debug.description: Adds additional log output to debug server side CORS issues.

path.description: The path to the pem file.

leak_sensitive_values.description: Logs sensitive values such as cookie and URL parameter.

format.description: Sets the log format.

serve.description: Controls the configuration for the http(s) daemon(s).

public.description: Controls the public daemon serving public API endpoints like /oauth2/auth, /oauth2/token, /.well-known/jwks.json

host.description: The interface or unix socket ORY Hydra should listen and handle public API requests on. Use the prefix "unix:" to specify a path to a unix socket. Leave empty to listen on all interfaces.

access_log.description: Access Log configuration for public server.

disable_for_health.description: Disable access log for health endpoints.

host.description: The interface or unix socket ORY Hydra should listen and handle administrative API requests on. Use the prefix "unix:" to specify a path to a unix socket. Leave empty to listen on all interfaces.

access_log.description: Access Log configuration for admin server.

disable_for_health.description: Disable access log for health endpoints.

tls.description: Configures HTTPS (HTTP over TLS). If configured, the server automatically supports HTTP/2.

key.description: Configures the private key (pem encoded).

allow_termination_from.description: Whitelist one or multiple CIDR address ranges and allow them to terminate TLS connections. Be aware that the X-Forwarded-Proto header must be set and must never be modifiable by anyone but your proxy / gateway / load balancer. Supports ipv4 and ipv6. Hydra serves http instead of https when this option is set.

same_site_mode.description: Specify the SameSite mode that cookies should be sent with.

same_site_legacy_workaround.description: Some older browser versions don’t work with SameSite=None. This option enables the workaround defined in https://web.dev/samesite-cookie-recipes/ which essentially stores a second cookie without SameSite as a fallback.

dsn.description: Sets the data source name. This configures the backend where ORY Hydra persists data. If dsn is "memory", data will be written to memory and is lost when you restart this instance. ORY Hydra supports popular SQL databases. For more detailed configuration information go to: https://www.ory.sh/docs/hydra/dependencies-environment#sql

broadcast_keys.description: A list of JSON Web Keys that should be exposed at that endpoint. This is usually the public key for verifying OpenID Connect ID Tokens. However, you might want to add additional keys here as well.

supported_claims.description: A list of supported claims to be broadcasted. Claim "sub" is always included.

supported_scope.description: The scope OAuth 2.0 Clients may request. Scope `offline`, `offline_access`, and `openid` are always included.

userinfo_url.description: A URL of the userinfo endpoint to be advertised at the OpenID Connect Discovery endpoint /.well-known/openid-configuration. Defaults to ORY Hydra's userinfo endpoint at /userinfo. Set this value if you want to handle this endpoint yourself.

subject_identifiers.description: Configures the Subject Identifier algorithm. For more information please head over to the documentation: https://www.ory.sh/docs/hydra/advanced#subject-identifier-algorithms

dynamic_client_registration.description: Configures OpenID Connect Dynamic Client Registration (exposed as admin endpoints /clients/...).

default_scope.description: The OpenID Connect Dynamic Client Registration specification has no concept of whitelisting OAuth 2.0 Scope. If you want to expose Dynamic Client Registration, you should set the default scope enabled for newly registered clients. Keep in mind that users can overwrite this default by setting the "scope" key in the registration payload, effectively disabling the concept of whitelisted scopes.

issuer.description: This value will be used as the "issuer" in access and ID tokens. It must be specified and using HTTPS protocol, unless --dangerous-force-http is set. This should typically be equal to the public value.

logout.description: Sets the logout endpoint. Defaults to an internal fallback URL.

post_logout_redirect.description: When a user agent requests to logout, it will be redirected to this url afterwards per default.

scope.description: Defines how scopes are matched. For more details have a look at https://github.com/ory/fosite#scopes

access_token.description: Defines access token type. jwt is a bad idea, see https://www.ory.sh/docs/hydra/advanced#json-web-tokens

login_consent_request.description: Configures how long a user login and consent flow may take.

access_token.description: Configures how long access tokens are valid.

system.description: The system secret must be at least 16 characters long. If none is provided, one will be generated. They key is used to encrypt sensitive data using AES-GCM (256 bit) and validate HMAC signatures. The first item in the list is used for signing and encryption. The whole list is used for verifying signatures and decryption.

cookie.description: A secret that is used to encrypt cookie sessions. Defaults to secrets.system. It is recommended to use a separate secret in production. The first item in the list is used for signing and encryption. The whole list is used for verifying signatures and decryption.

profiling.description: Enables profiling if set. For more details on profiling, head over to: https://blog.golang.org/profiling-go-programs

provider.description: Set this to the tracing backend you wish to use. Currently supports jaeger. If omitted or empty, tracing will be disabled.

local_agent_address.description: The address of the jaeger-agent where spans should be sent to.

schema.title: JSON schema for NPM package.json files

person.description: A person who has been involved in creating or maintaining this package

bundledDependency.description: Array of package names that will be bundled when publishing the package.

dependency.description: Dependencies are specified with a simple hash of package name to version range. The version range is a string which has one or more space-separated descriptors. Dependencies can also be identified with a tarball or git URL.

scriptsInstallAfter.description: Run AFTER the package is installed

scriptsPublishAfter.description: Run AFTER the package is published

scriptsRestart.description: Run by the 'npm restart' command. Note: 'npm restart' will run the stop and start scripts if no restart script is provided.

scriptsUninstallBefore.description: Run BEFORE the package is uninstalled

scriptsVersionBefore.description: Run BEFORE bump the package version

^_.description: Any property starting with _ is valid.

name.description: The name of the package.

version.description: Version must be parseable by node-semver, which is bundled with npm as a dependency.

description.description: This helps people discover your package, as it's listed in 'npm search'.

keywords.description: This helps people discover your package as it's listed in 'npm search'.

homepage.description: The url to the project homepage.

bugs.description: The url to your project's issue tracker and / or the email address to which issues should be reported. These are helpful for people who encounter issues with your package.

url.description: The url to your project's issue tracker.

email.description: The email address to which issues should be reported.

license.description: You should specify a license for your package so that people know how they are permitted to use it, and any restrictions you're placing on it.

licenses.description: You should specify a license for your package so that people know how they are permitted to use it, and any restrictions you're placing on it.

contributors.description: A list of people who contributed to this package.

maintainers.description: A list of people who maintains this package.

files.description: The 'files' field is an array of files to include in your project. If you name a folder in the array, then it will also include the files inside that folder.

main.description: The main field is a module ID that is the primary entry point to your program.

types.description: Set the types property to point to your bundled declaration file

typings.description: Note that the "typings" field is synonymous with "types", and could be used as well.

man.description: Specify either a single file or an array of filenames to put in place for the man program to find.

bin.description: If you specify a 'bin' directory, then all the files in that folder will be used as the 'bin' hash.

doc.description: Put markdown files in here. Eventually, these will be displayed nicely, maybe, someday.

example.description: Put example scripts in here. Someday, it might be exposed in some clever way.

lib.description: Tell people where the bulk of your library is. Nothing special is done with the lib folder in any way, but it's useful meta info.

man.description: A folder that is full of man pages. Sugar to generate a 'man' array by walking the folder.

repository.description: Specify the place where your code lives. This is helpful for people who want to contribute.

scripts.description: The 'scripts' member is an object hash of script commands that are run at various times in the lifecycle of your package. The key is the lifecycle event, and the value is the command to run at that point.

prepublish.description: Run BEFORE the package is published (Also run on local npm install without any arguments)

prepare.description: Run both BEFORE the package is packed and published, and on local npm install without any arguments. This is run AFTER prepublish, but BEFORE prepublishOnly

prepublishOnly.description: Run BEFORE the package is prepared and packed, ONLY on npm publish

prepack.description: run BEFORE a tarball is packed (on npm pack, npm publish, and when installing git dependencies)

postpack.description: Run AFTER the tarball has been generated and moved to its final destination.

preinstall.description: Run BEFORE the package is installed

postuninstall.description: Run AFTER the package is uninstalled

postversion.description: Run AFTER bump the package version

config.description: A 'config' hash can be used to set configuration parameters used in package scripts that persist across upgrades.

os.description: You can specify which operating systems your module will run on

cpu.description: If your code only runs on certain cpu architectures, you can specify which ones.

preferGlobal.description: If your package is primarily a command-line application that should be installed globally, then set this value to true to provide a warning if it is installed locally.

private.description: If set to true, then npm will refuse to publish it.

module.description: An ECMAScript module ID that is the primary entry point to your program.

esnext.description: A module ID with untranspiled code that is the primary entry point to your program.

@id.description: A string which represents a literal unique identifier for this model e.g. https://example.com/models/User

abstract.description: A boolean which indicates whether this model is an abstract model or not. The default value is false.

caching.description: A boolean which indicates whether model data will be cached or not. The default value is none -no caching-. A conditional caching allows developers to control caching mechanism while fetching data.

classPath.description: A string which represents a module path that exports a class which maps this database model e.g. './models/some-model'

description.description: A short description for this constraint e.g. Unique identifier field must be unique across different records.

type.description: A string which represents the type of this constraint e.g. unique

name.description: A string which the name of this event listener e.g. update person user listener

type.description: A string which represents the path of the module that exports this listener. This path may be a relative to execution folder path of a module exists in package modules e.g. ./listeners/add-user-listener or my-module/send-mail-listener

@id.description: A string which represents a literal unique identifier for this attribute e.g. https://example.com/models/attributes/name

calculation.description: An expression which represents the calculated value for this attribute.

description.description: A string which represents a short description of this attribute

editable.description: A boolean which indicates whether this attribute is editable or not.

expandable.description: A boolean value which indicates whether the associated object(s) will be automatically expanded or not.

indexed.description: A boolean which indicates whether this attribute is an indexed column or not.

many.description: A boolean value which indicates whether this attribute represents an one-to-many or many-to-many association between two models.

$expand.description: The set of expanded entities can be further refined through the application of expand options, expressed as a semicolon-separated list of system query options.

$levels.description: The value of the $levels system query option is a positive integer to specify the number of levels to expand e.g. $levels=2

$orderby.description: The $orderby system query option specifies the order in which items are returned from the service. e.g. $orderby=dateCreated desc

$select.description: The $select system query option requests that the service return only the properties, dynamic properties requested by the client e.g. $select=id,name,dateCreated

account.description: A string which represents the name of the security group where this privilege will be applied e.g. Administrators, Sales etc.

filter.description: A string which represents a filter expression for this privilege. This attribute is used for self privileges which are commonly derived from user's attributes e.g. 'owner eq me()' or 'orderStatus eq 1 and customer eq me()' etc.

mask.description: A number which represents permission mask (1=Read, 2=Create, 4=Update, 8=Delete, 16=Execute)

type.description: A string which represents the permission scope.

name.description: A string which represents the name of this attribute e.g. title, description, dateCreated etc

nested.description: A boolean which indicates whether this attribute defines an association between two models where child objects are always treated as a part of the parent object.

nullable.description: A boolean which indicates whether this attribute is nullable or not.

primary.description: A boolean which indicates whether this attribute is a key column or not.

property.description: A string which optionally represents the name of this attribute in object mapping. This name may defer from the name of the database field.

readonly.description: A boolean which indicates whether this attribute is readonly or not. A readonly value must have a default value or a calculated value.

size.description: A number which represents the maximum size for this attribute e.g. the size of a text field etc

message.description: A string which represents a message that is going to be used when validation fails.

minLength.description: Sets a value which represents the min length.

minValue.description: Sets a value which represents the min value.

pattern.description: A string which represents a regular expression that validates values of this attribute.

patternMessage.description: A string which represents a message that is going to be used when pattern validation fails.

validator.description: A string which represetns the module path that exports a custom validator e.g. ./validators/custom-validator.js

value.description: An expression which represents the default value for this attribute.

hidden.description: A boolean which indicates whether this model is hidden or not. The default value is false.

id.description: An optional numeric identifier for this model e.g. 9587891

implements.description: A string which represents the model which is implemented by this model e.g. ActionStatusType model implements Enumeration model etc

schema.title: Gitlab CI configuration
schema.description: Gitlab has a built-in solution for doing CI called Gitlab CI. It is configured by supplying a file called `.gitlab-ci.yml`, which will list all the jobs that are going to run for the project. A full list of all options can be found at https://docs.gitlab.com/ee/ci/yaml/. You can read more about Gitlab CI at https://docs.gitlab.com/ee/ci/README.html.

stages.description: Groups jobs into stages. All jobs in one stage must complete before next stage is executed. Defaults to ['build', 'test', 'deploy'].

include.description: Can be string or array of strings which should be an URL or local file reference (e.g. '/templates/ci-template.yml'). The external content will be fetched, included and evaluated along the `.gitlab-ci.yml`.

pages.description: A special job used to upload static sites to Gitlab pages. Requires a `public/` directory with `artifacts.path` pointing to it.

oneOf.description: Full name of the image that should be used. It should contain the Registry part if needed.
Specifies the docker image to use for the job or globally for all jobs. Job configuration takes precedence over global setting. Requires a certain kind of Gitlab runner executor.

name.description: Full name of the image that should be used. It should contain the Registry part if needed.

entrypoint.description: Command or script that should be executed as the container's entrypoint. It will be translated to Docker's --entrypoint option while creating the container. The syntax is similar to Dockerfile's ENTRYPOINT directive, where each shell token is a separate string in the array.

image.description: Specifies the docker image to use for the job or globally for all jobs. Job configuration takes precedence over global setting. Requires a certain kind of Gitlab runner executor.

services.description: Similar to `image` property, but will link the specified services to the `image` container.

oneOf.description: Full name of the image that should be used. It should contain the Registry part if needed.

name.description: Full name of the image that should be used. It should contain the Registry part if needed.

entrypoint.description: Command or script that should be executed as the container's entrypoint. It will be translated to Docker's --entrypoint option while creating the container. The syntax is similar to Dockerfile's ENTRYPOINT directive, where each shell token is a separate string in the array.

command.description: Command or script that should be used as the container's command. It will be translated to arguments passed to Docker after the image's name. The syntax is similar to Dockerfile's CMD directive, where each shell token is a separate string in the array.

alias.description: Additional alias that can be used to access the service from the job's container. Read Accessing the services for more information.

before_script.description: Defines scripts that should run *before* the job. Can be set globally or per job.

after_script.description: Defines scripts that should run *after* the job. Can be set globally or per job.

variables.description: Defines environment variables for specific jobs or globally. Job level property overrides global variables. If a job sets `variables: {}`, all global variables are turned off.

cache.description: Specify files or directories to cache between jobs. Can be set globally or per job.

paths.description: List of files or paths to cache.

key.description: Unique cache ID, to allow e.g. specific branch or job cache. Environment variables can be used to set up unique keys (e.g. "$CI_COMMIT_REF_SLUG" for per branch cache).

untracked.description: Set to `true` to cache untracked files.

policy.description: Determines the strategy for downloading and updating the cache.

oneOf.description: Pull will download cache but skip uploading after job completes.
Push will skip downloading cache and always recreate cache after job completes.
Pull-push will both download cache at job start and upload cache on job success.

filter_refs.description: Filter job by different keywords that determine origin or state, or by supplying string/regex to check against branch/tag names.

oneOf.description: When a branch is pushed.
When a tag is pushed.
When a pipeline has been triggered by a second pipelines API (not triggers API).
When using CI services other than Gitlab
For multi-project triggers, created using the API with 'CI_JOB_TOKEN'.
Pipeline is triggered by a `git push` by the user
For scheduled pipelines.
For pipelines created using a trigger token.
For pipelines created using *Run pipeline* button in Gitlab UI (under your project's *Pipelines*).

anyOf.description: String or regular expression to match against tag or branch names.

kubernetes.description: Filter job based on if Kubernetes integration is active.

variables.description: Filter job by checking comparing values of environment variables. Read more about variable expressions: https://docs.gitlab.com/ee/ci/variables/README.html#variables-expressions

changes.description: Filter job creation based on files that were modified in a git push.

retry_max.description: The number of times the job will be retried if it fails. Defaults to 0 and can max be retried 2 times (3 times total).

oneOf.description: Retry on any failure (default).
Retry when the failure reason is unknown.
Retry when the script failed.
Retry on API failure.
Retry when the job got stuck or timed out.
Retry if there was a runner system failure (e.g. setting up the job failed).
Retry if a dependency was missing.
Retry if the runner was unsupported.

script.description: Shell scripts executed by the Runner. The only required property of jobs. Be careful with special characters (e.g. `:`, `{`, `}`, `&`) and use single or double quotes to avoid issues.

stage.description: Define what stage the job will run in.

only.description: Job will run *only* when these filtering options match.

extends.description: The name of a job to inherit configuration from.

except.description: Job will run *except* for when these filtering options match.

tags.description: Used to select runners from the list of available runners. A runner must have all tags listed here to run the job.

allow_failure.description: Setting this option to true will allow the job to fail while still letting the pipeline pass.

when.description: Describes the conditions for when to run the job. Defaults to 'on_success'.

oneOf.description: Execute job only when all jobs from prior stages succeed.
Execute job when at least one job from prior stages fails.
Execute job regardless of the status from prior stages.
Execute the job manually from Gitlab UI or API. Read more: https://docs.gitlab.com/ee/ci/yaml/#when-manual
Execute a job after the time limit in 'start_in' expires. Read more: https://docs.gitlab.com/ee/ci/yaml/#when-delayed

start_in.description: Used in conjunction with 'when: delayed' to set how long to delay before starting a job.

dependencies.description: Specify a list of job names from earlier stages from which artifacts should be loaded. By default, all previous artifacts are passed. Use an empty array to skip downloading artifacts.

artifacts.description: Used to specify a list of files and directories that should be attached to the job if it succeeds. Artifacts are sent to Gitlab where they can be downloaded.

paths.description: A list of paths to files/folders that should be included in the artifact.

name.description: Name for the archive created on job success. Can use variables in the name, e.g. '$CI_JOB_NAME'

untracked.description: Whether to add all untracked files (along with 'artifacts.paths') to the artifact.

when.description: Configure when artifacts are uploaded depended on job status.

oneOf.description: Upload artifacts only when the job succeeds (this is the default).
Upload artifacts only when the job fails.
Upload artifacts regardless of job status.

expire_in.description: How long artifacts should be kept. They are saved 30 days by default. Artifacts that have expired are removed periodically via cron job. Supports a wide variety of formats, e.g. '1 week', '3 mins 4 sec', '2 hrs 20 min', '2h20min', '6 mos 1 day', '47 yrs 6 mos and 4d', '3 weeks and 2 days'.

reports.description: Reports will be uploaded as artifacts, and often displayed in the Gitlab UI, such as in Merge Requests.

junit.description: Path for file(s) that should be parsed as JUnit XML result

oneOf.description: Path to a single XML file
A list of paths to XML files that will automatically be concatenated into a single file

codequality.description: Path to file or list of files with code quality report(s) (such as Code Climate).

sast.description: Path to file or list of files with SAST vulnerabilities report(s).

dependency_scanning.description: Path to file or list of files with Dependency scanning vulnerabilities report(s).

container_scanning.description: Path to file or list of files with Container scanning vulnerabilities report(s).

dast.description: Path to file or list of files with DAST vulnerabilities report(s).

license_management.description: Path to file or list of files with license report(s).

performance.description: Path to file or list of files with performance metrics report(s).

environment.description: Used to associate environment metadata with a deploy. Environment can have a name and URL attached to it, and will be displayed under /environments under the project.

name.description: The name of the environment, e.g. 'qa', 'staging', 'production'.

url.description: When set, this will expose buttons in various places for the current environment in Gitlab, that will take you to the defined URL.

on_stop.description: The name of a job to execute when the environment is about to be stopped.

action.description: Stops this environment so that it is inactive.

coverage.description: Must be a regular expression, optionally but recommended to be quoted, and must be surrounded with '/'. Example: '/Code coverage: \d+\.\d+/'

retry.description: Retry a job if it fails. Can be a simple integer or object definition.

when.description: Either a single or array of error types to trigger job retry.

parallel.description: Parallel will split up a single job into several, and provide `CI_NODE_INDEX` and `CI_NODE_TOTAL` environment variables for the running jobs.

schema.title: Prometheus
schema.description: Prometheus configuration file

global.description: The global configuration specifies parameters that are valid in all other configuration contexts. They also serve as defaults for other configuration sections.

scrape_interval.description: How frequently to scrape targets by default.

scrape_timeout.description: How long until a scrape request times out.

external_labels.description: The labels to add to any time series or alerts when communicating with external systems (federation, remote storage, Alertmanager).

rule_files.description: Rule files specifies a list of globs. Rules and alerts are read from all matching files.

remote_write.description: Settings related to the remote write feature.

url.description: The URL of the endpoint to send samples to.

remote_timeout.description: Timeout for requests to the remote write endpoint.

write_relabel_configs.description: List of remote write relabel configurations.

tls_config.description: Configures the remote write request's TLS settings.

queue_config.description: Configures the queue used to write to remote storage.

capacity.description: Number of samples to buffer per shard before we block reading of more samples from the WAL. It is recommended to have enough capacity in each shard to buffer several requests to keep throughput up while processing occasional slow remote requests.

max_shards.description: Maximum number of shards, i.e. amount of concurrency.

min_shards.description: Minimum number of shards, i.e. amount of concurrency.

max_samples_per_send.description: Maximum number of samples per send.

batch_send_deadline.description: Maximum time a sample will wait in buffer.

min_backoff.description: Initial retry delay. Gets doubled for every retry.

remote_read.description: Settings related to the remote read feature.

url.description: The URL of the endpoint to query from.

required_matchers.description: An optional list of equality matchers which have to be present in a selector to query the remote read endpoint.

remote_timeout.description: Timeout for requests to the remote read endpoint.

read_recent.description: Whether reads should be made for queries for time ranges that the local storage should have complete data for.

job_name.description: The job name assigned to scraped metrics by default. Must be unique across all scrape configurations.

scrape_interval.description: How frequently to scrape targets from this job. Defaults to `global.scrape_interval`.

scrape_timeout.description: Per-scrape timeout when scraping this job. Defaults to `global.scrape_timeout`.

metrics_path.description: The HTTP resource path on which to fetch metrics from targets.

honor_labels.description: Controls how Prometheus handles conflicts between labels that are already present in scraped data and labels that Prometheus would attach server-side ("job" and "instance" labels, manually configured target labels, and labels generated by service discovery implementations).

honor_timestamps.description: Controls whether Prometheus respects the timestamps present in scraped data.

scheme.description: Configures the protocol scheme used for requests.

tls_config.description: Configures the scrape request's TLS settings.

sample_limit.description: Per-scrape limit on number of scraped samples that will be accepted. If more than this number of samples are present after metric relabelling the entire scrape will be treated as failed. 0 means no limit.

alerting.description: Alerting specifies settings related to the Alertmanager.

timeout.description: Per-target Alertmanager timeout when pushing alerts.

path_prefix.description: Prefix for the HTTP path alerts are pushed to.

scheme.description: Configures the protocol scheme used for requests.

tls_config.description: Configures the scrape request's TLS settings.

basic_auth.description: Sets the `Authorization` header on every remote write request with the configured username and password. password and password_file are mutually exclusive.

bearer_token.description: Sets the `Authorization` header on every scrape request with the configured bearer token. It is mutually exclusive with `bearer_token_file`.

bearer_token_file.description: Sets the `Authorization` header on every scrape request with the bearer token read from the configured file. It is mutually exclusive with `bearer_token`.

source_labels.description: The source labels select values from existing labels. Their content is concatenated using the configured separator and matched against the configured regular expression for the replace, keep, and drop actions.

separator.description: Separator placed between concatenated source label values.

target_label.description: Label to which the resulting value is written in a replace action. It is mandatory for replace actions. Regex capture groups are available.
target_label.$comment: https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/release-2.13/config/testdata/conf.good.yml#L146 has a regex capture group, violating vanilla label_name definition.

regex.description: Regular expression against which the extracted value is matched.

modulus.description: Modulus to take of the hash of the source label values.

replacement.description: Replacement value against which a regex replace is performed if the regular expression matches. Regex capture groups are available.

action.description: Action to perform based on regex matching.

ca_file.description: CA certificate to validate API server certificate with.

cert_file.description: Certificate file for client cert authentication to the server.

key_file.description: Key file for client cert authentication to the server.

server_name.description: ServerName extension to indicate the name of the server.

insecure_skip_verify.description: Disable validation of the server certificate.

azure_sd_configs.description: List of Azure service discovery configurations.

schema.title: GeoJSON Object
schema.description: This object represents a geometry, feature, or collection of features.

type.title: Type
type.description: The type of GeoJSON object.

crs.title: Coordinate Reference System (CRS)
crs.description:
The coordinate reference system (CRS) of a GeoJSON object is determined by its `crs` member (referred to as the CRS object below). If an object has no crs member, then its parent or grandparent object's crs member may be acquired. If no crs member can be so acquired, the default CRS shall apply to the GeoJSON object.

* The default CRS is a geographic coordinate reference system, using the WGS84 datum, and with longitude and latitude units of decimal degrees.

* The value of a member named `crs` must be a JSON object (referred to as the CRS object below) or JSON null. If the value of CRS is null, no CRS can be assumed.

* The crs member should be on the top-level GeoJSON object in a hierarchy (in feature collection, feature, geometry order) and should not be repeated or overridden on children or grandchildren of the object.

* A non-null CRS object has two mandatory members: `type` and `properties`.

* The value of the type member must be a string, indicating the type of CRS object.

* The value of the properties member must be an object.

* CRS shall not change coordinate ordering.

type.title: CRS Type
type.description: The value of the type member must be a string, indicating the type of CRS object.

href.title: href
href.description: The value of the required `href` member must be a dereferenceable URI.

type.title: Link Object Type
type.description: The value of the optional `type` member must be a string that hints at the format used to represent CRS parameters at the provided URI. Suggested values are: `proj4`, `ogcwkt`, `esriwkt`, but others can be used.

bbox.title: Bounding Box
bbox.description: To include information on the coordinate range for geometries, features, or feature collections, a GeoJSON object may have a member named `bbox`. The value of the bbox member must be a 2*n array where n is the number of dimensions represented in the contained geometries, with the lowest values for all axes followed by the highest values. The axes order of a bbox follows the axes order of geometries. In addition, the coordinate reference system for the bbox is assumed to match the coordinate reference system of the GeoJSON object of which it is a member.

oneOf.title: Point
oneOf.description: For type `Point`, the `coordinates` member must be a single position.

oneOf.title: Multi Point Geometry
oneOf.description: For type `MultiPoint`, the `coordinates` member must be an array of positions.

oneOf.title: Line String
oneOf.description:
For type `LineString`, the `coordinates` member must be an array of two or more positions.

A LinearRing is closed LineString with 4 or more positions. The first and last positions are equivalent (they represent equivalent points). Though a LinearRing is not explicitly represented as a GeoJSON geometry type, it is referred to in the Polygon geometry type definition.

oneOf.title: MultiLineString
oneOf.description: For type `MultiLineString`, the `coordinates` member must be an array of LineString coordinate arrays.

oneOf.title: Polygon
oneOf.description: For type `Polygon`, the `coordinates` member must be an array of LinearRing coordinate arrays. For Polygons with multiple rings, the first must be the exterior ring and any others must be interior rings or holes.

oneOf.title: Multi-Polygon Geometry
oneOf.description: For type `MultiPolygon`, the `coordinates` member must be an array of Polygon coordinate arrays.

oneOf.title: Geometry Collection
oneOf.description:
A GeoJSON object with type `GeometryCollection` is a geometry object which represents a collection of geometry objects.

A geometry collection must have a member with the name `geometries`. The value corresponding to `geometries` is an array. Each element in this array is a GeoJSON geometry object.

geometry.title: Geometry
geometry.description: A geometry is a GeoJSON object where the type member's value is one of the following strings: `Point`, `MultiPoint`, `LineString`, `MultiLineString`, `Polygon`, `MultiPolygon`, or `GeometryCollection`.

feature.title: Feature
feature.description:
A GeoJSON object with the type `Feature` is a feature object.

* A feature object must have a member with the name `geometry`. The value of the geometry member is a geometry object as defined above or a JSON null value.

* A feature object must have a member with the name `properties`. The value of the properties member is an object (any JSON object or a JSON null value).

* If a feature has a commonly used identifier, that identifier should be included as a member of the feature object with the name `id`.

featurecollection.title: Feature Collection
featurecollection.description:
A GeoJSON object with the type `FeatureCollection` is a feature collection object.

An object of type `FeatureCollection` must have a member with the name `features`. The value corresponding to `features` is an array. Each element in the array is a feature object as defined above.

linearRingCoordinates.title: Linear Ring Coordinates
linearRingCoordinates.description: A LinearRing is closed LineString with 4 or more positions. The first and last positions are equivalent (they represent equivalent points). Though a LinearRing is not explicitly represented as a GeoJSON geometry type, it is referred to in the Polygon geometry type definition.

lineStringCoordinates.title: Line String Coordinates
lineStringCoordinates.description: For type `LineString`, the `coordinates` member must be an array of two or more positions.

polygonCoordinates.title: Polygon Coordinates
polygonCoordinates.description: For type `Polygon`, the `coordinates` member must be an array of LinearRing coordinate arrays. For Polygons with multiple rings, the first must be the exterior ring and any others must be interior rings or holes.

position.title: Position
position.description:
A position is the fundamental geometry construct. The `coordinates` member of a geometry object is composed of one position (in the case of a Point geometry), an array of positions (LineString or MultiPoint geometries), an array of arrays of positions (Polygons, MultiLineStrings), or a multidimensional array of positions (MultiPolygon).

A position is represented by an array of numbers. There must be at least two elements, and may be more. The order of elements must follow x, y, z order (easting, northing, altitude for coordinates in a projected coordinate reference system, or longitude, latitude, altitude for coordinates in a geographic coordinate reference system). Any number of additional elements are allowed -- interpretation and meaning of additional elements is beyond the scope of this specification.

schema.description:
This object contains information about the channel representation in AMQP.
See https://github.com/asyncapi/bindings/tree/master/amqp#channel-binding-object.

is.description: Defines what type of channel is it. Can be either `queue` or `routingKey` (default).

bindingVersion.description: The version of this binding. If omitted, "latest" MUST be assumed.

allOf.description: Queue and exchange are mutually exclusive.

exchange.description: When `is`=`routingKey`, this object defines the exchange properties.

name.description: The name of the exchange. It MUST NOT exceed 255 characters long.

type.description: The type of the exchange. Can be either `topic`, `direct`, `fanout`, `default` or `headers`.

durable.description: Whether the exchange should survive broker restarts or not.

autoDelete.description: Whether the exchange should be deleted when the last queue is unbound from it.

queue.description: When `is`=`queue`, this object defines the queue properties.

name.description: The name of the queue. It MUST NOT exceed 255 characters long.

durable.description: Whether the queue should survive broker restarts or not.

exclusive.description: Whether the queue should be used only by one connection or not.

autoDelete.description: Whether the queue should be deleted when the last consumer unsubscribes.

openrtb-v2_1-schema-bid_request
schema.description: json schema for an openrtb v2.1 bid request (http://www.iab.net/media/file/OpenRTB-API-Specification-Version-2-1-FINAL.pdf)

id.title: Id (id)
id.description: Unique ID of the bid request, provided by the exchange.

imp.title: Impressions (impressions)
imp.description: Array of impression objects. Multiple impression auctions may be specified in a single bid request. At least one impression is required for a valid bid request.

site.title: Publisher Site (site)
site.description: Publisher site definition.  A bid request must not contain both a site object and an app object.

app.title: Publishing Application (app)
app.description: Publisher application definition.  A bid request must not contain both a site object and an app object.

at.title: Auction type (at)
at.description: If “1”, then first price auction. If “2”, then second price auction. Additional auction types can be defined as per the exchange’s business rules.  Exchange specific rules should be numbered over 500

tmax.title: Maximum Bid Time (tmax)
tmax.description: Maximum amount of time in milliseconds to submit a bid (e.g., 120 means the bidder has 120ms to submit a bid before the auction is complete). If this value never changes across an exchange, then the exchange can supply this information offline.

wseat.title: Buyer Seats (wseat)
wseat.description: Array of buyer seats allowed to bid on this auction. Seats are an optional feature of exchange. For example, ['4','34','82','A45'] indicates that only advertisers using these exchange seats are allowed to bid on the impressions in this auction

allimps.title: All Impression Availability (allimps)
allimps.description: Flag to indicate whether Exchange can verify that all impressions offered represent all of the impressions available in context (e.g., all impressions available on the web page; all impressions available for a video [pre, mid and postroll spots], etc.) to support road-blocking. A true value should only be passed if the exchange is aware of all impressions in context for the publisher. '0' means the exchange cannot verify, and '1' means that all impressions represent all impressions available.

cur.title: Currencies (cur)
cur.description: Array of allowed currencies for bids on this bid request using ISO-4217 alphabetic codes. If only one currency is used by the exchange, this parameter is not required.

bcat.title: Blocked Advertiser Categories (bcat)
bcat.description: Blocked Advertiser Categories. Note that there is no existing categorization / taxonomy of advertiser industries. However, as a substitute exchanges may decide to use IAB categories as an approximation (See Table 6.1 Content Categories)

badv.title: Blocked Advertiser Domains (badv)
badv.description: Array of strings of blocked toplevel domains of advertisers. For example, {'company1.com', 'company2.com'}

ext.title: Custom JSON (ext)
ext.description: This object is a placeholder that may contain custom JSON agreed to by the parties in an OpenRTB transaction to support flexibility beyond the standard defined in this specification.

id.title: Impression Id (id)
id.description: A unique identifier for this impression within the context of the bid request (typically, value starts with 1, and increments up to n for n impressions)

banner.title: A banner object (banner)
banner.description: A reference to a banner object. Either a banner or video object(or both if the impression could be either) must be included in an impression object

video.title: A video object (video)
video.description: A reference to a video object. Either a banner or video object (or both if the impression could be either) must be included in an impression object.

displaymanager.title: Video/Native display manager (displaymanager)
displaymanager.description: Name of ad mediation partner, SDK technology, or native player responsible for rendering ad (typically video or mobile). Used by some ad servers to customize ad code by partner.

displaymanagerver.title: Video/Native display manager version (displaymanagerver)
displaymanagerver.description: Version of ad mediation partner, SDK technology, or native player responsible for rendering ad (typically video or mobile). Used by some ad servers to customize ad code by partner

instl.title: Interstitial/Full Screen (instl)
instl.description: 1 if the ad is interstitial or full screen; else 0 (i.e., no).

tagid.title: Tag id (tagid)
tagid.description: Identifier for specific ad placement or ad tag that was used to initiate the auction. This can be useful for debugging of any issues, or for optimization by the buyer.

bidfloor.title: Bid Floor (bidfloor)
bidfloor.description: Bid floor for this impression (in CPM of bidfloorcur).

bidfloorcur.title: Bid Floor Currency (bidfloorcur)
bidfloorcur.description: If bid floor is specified and multiple currencies supported per bid request, then currency should be specified here using ISO-4217 alphabetic codes. Note, this may be different from bid currency returned by bidder, if this is allowed on an exchange.

iframebuster.title: Iframe Buster Names (iframebuster)
iframebuster.description: Array of names for supported iframe busters. Exchange specific.

ext.title: Custom JSON (ext)
ext.description: This object is a placeholder that may contain custom JSON agreed to by the parties in an OpenRTB transaction to support flexibility beyond the standard defined in this specification.

w.title: Width (w)
w.description: Width of the impression in pixels. Since some ad types are not restricted by size this field is not required, but it’s highly recommended that this information be included when possible.

h.title: Height (h)
h.description: Height of the impression in pixels. Since some ad types are not restricted by size this field is not required, but it’s highly recommended that this information be included when possible.

id.title: Banner Id (id)
id.description: Unique identifier for this banner object. Useful for tracking multiple banner objects (e.g., in companion banner array). Usually starts with 1, increasing with each object. Combination of impression id banner object should be unique.

btype.title: Blocked Creative Types (btype)
btype.description: Blocked creative types. See Table 6.2 Banner Ad Types. If blank, assume all types are allowed.

battr.title: Blocked Creative Attributes (battr)
battr.description: Blocked creative attributes. See Table 6.3 Creative Attributes. If blank assume all types are allowed.

mimes.title: Mime type whitelist (mimes)
mimes.description: Whitelist of content MIME types supported. Popular MIME types include, but are not limited to 'image/jpg', 'image/gif' and 'application/x-shockwave-flash'

topframe.title: Delivery frame (topframe)
topframe.description: Specify if the banner is delivered in the top frame or in an iframe. '0' means it is not in the top frame, and '1' means that it is.

expdir.title: Expandable properties (expdir)
expdir.description: Specify properties for an expandable ad. See Table 6.11 Expandable Direction for possible values.

api.title: Supported API frameworks (api)
api.description: List of supported API frameworks for this banner. (See Table 6.4 API Frameworks). If an API is not explicitly listed it is assumed not to be supported.

ext.title: Custom JSON (ext)
ext.description: This object is a placeholder that may contain custom JSON agreed to by the parties in an OpenRTB transaction to support flexibility beyond the standard defined in this specification.

mimes.title: Mime type whitelist (mimes)
mimes.description: Content MIME types supported. Popular MIME types include, but are not limited to 'video/x-mswmv' for Windows Media, and 'video/x-flv' for Flash Video.

linearity.title: Video Linearity (linearity)
linearity.description: Indicates whether the ad impression is linear or non-linear. See Table 6.6 Video Linearity for a list of the possible values

minduration.title: Minimum Duration (minduration)
minduration.description: Minimum video ad duration in seconds

maxduration.title: Maximum Duration (maxduration)
maxduration.description: Maximum video ad duration in seconds

protocol.title: Protocol (protocol)
protocol.description: Video bid response protocols.  See Table 6.7 Video Bid Response Protocols for a list of possible values

w.title: Player Width (w)
w.description: Width of the player in pixels. This field is not required, but it’s highly recommended that this information be included.

h.title: Player Height (h)
h.description: Height of the player in pixels. This field is not required, but it’s highly recommended that this information be included.

startdelay.title: Start Delay (startdelay)
startdelay.description: Indicates the start delay in seconds for preroll, midroll, or postroll ad placement. See Table 6.9 Video Start Delay for generic placement values

sequence.title: Ad Sequency (sequence)
sequence.description: If multiple ad impressions are offered in the same bid request, the sequence number will allow for the coordinated delivery of multiple creatives

battr.title: Blocked creative attributes (battr)
battr.description: Blocked creative attributes. See Table 6.3 Creative Attributes. If blank assume all types are allowed.

maxextended.title: Maximum extended duration (maxextended)
maxextended.description: Maximum extended video ad duration, if extension is allowed.  If blank or 0, extension is not allowed. If -1, extension is allowed, and there is no time limit imposed. If greater than 0, then the value represents the number of seconds of extended play supported beyond the maxduration value.

minbitrate.title: Minimum bitrate (minbitrate)
minbitrate.description: Minimum bit rate in Kbps. Exchange may set this dynamically, or universally across their set of publishers.

maxbitrate.title: Maximum bitrate (maxbitrate)
maxbitrate.description: Maximum bit rate in Kbps. Exchange may set this dynamically, or universally across their set of publishers.

boxingallowed.title: Boxing (boxingallowed)
boxingallowed.description: If exchange publisher has rules preventing letter boxing of 4x3 content to play in a 16x9 window, then this should be set to false. Default setting is true, which assumes that boxing of content to fit into a window is allowed. '1' indicates boxing is allowed. '0' indicates it is not allowed.

playbackmethod.title: Playback methods (playbackmethod)
playbackmethod.description: List of allowed playback methods. If blank, assume that all are allowed. See Table 6.8 Video Playback Methods for a list of possible values.

delivery.title: Delivery methods (delivery)
delivery.description: List of supported delivery methods (streaming, progressive). If blank, assume all are supported. See Table 6.12 Content Delivery Methods for a list of possible values.

companionad.title: Companion Ads (companionad)
companionad.description: If companion ads are available, they can be listed as an array of banner objects. See Banner Object.

api.title: Supported APIs (api)
api.description: List of supported API frameworks for this impression. (See Table 6.4 API Frameworks). If an API is not explicitly listed it is assumed not to be supported.

companiontype.title: Companion Types (companiontype)
companiontype.description: Recommended if companion objects are included. See Table 6.17 VAST Companion Types for a list of possible values.

ext.title: Custom JSON (ext)
ext.description: This object is a placeholder that may contain custom JSON agreed to by the parties in an OpenRTB transaction to support flexibility beyond the standard defined in this specification.

id.title: Site Id (id)
id.description: Site ID on the exchange

name.title: Site Name (name)
name.description: Site name (may be masked at publisher’s request).

domain.title: Site Domain (domain)
domain.description: Domain of the site, used for advertiser side blocking. For example, 'foo.com'.

cat.title: Site Categories (cat)
cat.description: Array of IAB content categories for the overall site. See Table 6.1 Content Categories.

sectioncat.title: Site Section Categories (sectioncat)
sectioncat.description: Array of IAB content categories for the current subsection of the site. See Table 6.1 Content Categories.

pagecat.title: Page Categories (pagecat)
pagecat.description: Array of IAB content categories for the current page. See Table 6.1 Content Categories.

page.title: Page URL (page)
page.description: URL of the page where the impression will be shown.

privacypolicy.title: Privacy Policy (privacypolicy)
privacypolicy.description: Specifies whether the site has a privacy policy. '1' means there is a policy. '0' means there is not.

ref.title: Referal URL (ref)
ref.description: Referrer URL that caused navigation to the current page.

search.title: Search String (search)
search.description: Search string that caused navigation to the current page.

keywords.title: Keywords (keywords)
keywords.description: List of keywords describing this site in a comma separated string.

ext.description: This object is a placeholder that may contain custom JSON agreed to by the parties in an OpenRTB transaction to support flexibility beyond the standard defined in this specification.

id.title: App Id (id)
id.description: Application ID on the exchange.

name.title: App Name (name)
name.description: Application name (may be masked at publisher’s request).

domain.title: App Domain Name (domain)
domain.description: Domain of the application (e.g., 'mygame.foo.com').

cat.title: App Categories (cat)
cat.description: Array of IAB content categories for the overall application. See Table 6.1 Content Categories.

sectioncat.title: App Section Categories (sectioncat)
sectioncat.description: Array of IAB content categories for the current subsection of the app. See Table 6.1 Content Categories.

pagecat.title: App Page/View Categories (pagecat)
pagecat.description: Array of IAB content categories for the current page/view of the app. See Table 6.1 Content Categories.

bundle.title: App Bundle (bundle)
bundle.description: Application bundle or package name (e.g., com.foo.mygame). This is intended to be a unique ID across multiple exchanges.

privacypolicy.title: App Privacy Policy (privacypolicy)
privacypolicy.description: Specifies whether the app has a privacy policy. '1' means there is a policy and '0' means there is not

paid.title: App Type (paid)
paid.description: '1' if the application is a paid version; else '0' (i.e., free).

keywords.title: Keywords (keywords)
keywords.description: List of keywords describing this app in a comma separated string

storeurl.title: App Store URL (storeurl)
storeurl.description: For QAG 1.5 compliance, an app store URL for an installed app should be passed in the bid request.

ext.title: Custom JSON (ext)
ext.description: This object is a placeholder that may contain custom JSON agreed to by the parties in an OpenRTB transaction to support flexibility beyond the standard defined in this specification.

id.title: Content Id (id)
id.description: ID uniquely identifying the content

episode.title: Episode Number (episode)
episode.description: Content episode number (typically applies to video content).

title.title: Title (title)
title.description: Content title. Video examples: 'Search Committee' (television) or 'A New Hope' (movie) or 'Endgame' (made for web) Non-video example: 'Why an Antarctic Glacier Is Melting So Quickly' (Time magazine article)

series.title: Series (series)
series.description: Content series. Video examples: 'The Office' (television) or 'Star Wars' (movie) or 'Arby ‘N’ The Chief' (made for web) Non-video example: 'Ecocentric' (Time magazine blog)

season.title: Season (season)
season.description: Content season. E.g., 'Season 3' (typically applies to video content).

url.title: URL (url)
url.description: Original URL of the content, for buy-side contextualization or review

cat.title: Categories (cat)
cat.description: Array of IAB content categories for the content. See Table 6.1 Content Categories.

videoquality.title: Video Quality (videoquality)
videoquality.description: Video quality per the IAB’s classification. See Table 6.14 Video Quality.

keywords.title: Keywords (keywords)
keywords.description: Comma separated list of keywords describing the content

userrating.title: User Rating (userrating)
userrating.description: User rating of the content (e.g., number of stars, likes, etc.).

context.title: Type (context)
context.description: Specifies the type of content (game, video, text, etc.). See Table 6.13 Content Context.

livestream.title: Live (livestream)
livestream.description: Is content live? E.g., live video stream, live blog. '1' means content is live. '0' means it is not live.

len.title: Length in seconds (len)
len.description: Length of content (appropriate for video or audio) in seconds.

qagmediarating.title: QAG rating (qagmediarating)
qagmediarating.description: Media rating of the content, per QAG guidelines. See Table 0 QAG Media Ratings for list of possible values

embeddable.title: Embedability (embeddable)
embeddable.description: From QAG Video Addendum. If content can be embedded (such as an embeddable video player) this value should be set to '1'. If content cannot be embedded, then this should be set to '0'.

language.title: Content language (language)
language.description: Language of the content. Use alpha-2/ISO 639-1 codes

id.title: Publisher Id (id)
id.description: Publisher ID on the exchange

name.title: Publisher Name (name)
name.description: Publisher name (may be masked at publisher’s request).

cat.title: Publisher Categories (cat)
cat.description: Array of IAB content categories for the publisher. See Table 6.1 Content Categories.

domain.title: Publisher Domain (domain)
domain.description: Publisher’s highest level domain name, for example 'foopub.com'.

ext.description: This object is a placeholder that may contain custom JSON agreed to by the parties in an OpenRTB transaction to support flexibility beyond the standard defined in this specification.

id.title: Producer Id (id)
id.description: Content producer or originator ID. Useful if content is syndicated, and may be posted on a site using embed tags

name.title: Producer Name (name)
name.description: Content producer or originator name (e.g., 'Warner Bros').

cat.title: Producer Categories (cat)
cat.description: Array of IAB content categories for the content producer. See Table 6.1 Content Categories.

domain.title: URL (domain)
domain.description: URL of the content producer.
